subject: Region pin pledge and subprocessor sequencing plan
messages:
From: Samantha Liao <samantha.liao@medicore.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: legal@medicore.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Residency ask: sequencing of subprocessors + region-pin pledge

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Two short asks to close the loop so our InfoSec & Procurement teams can move the DPA forward:

1) Can Redwood provide a written pledge describing the sequencing/order in which new subprocessors will be activated for our account (we need an assurance we will be notified and have a 10-business-day window for vetting before activation to production)?
2) We need a firm statement of region-pinning commitments for Prod data: can you confirm primary regions for EU, US, and APAC and the maximum transient-egress window you permit for emergency failover?

We're attaching our updated redlines for the DPA (Medicore_DPA_redline_v3.pdf) — the legal team will flag any gaps against your pledge.

Appreciate a short note confirming behaviors and a proposed sequencing bullet list.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Liao
Head of Cloud Security, Medicore Health

Attachments: Medicore_DPA_redline_v3.pdf
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Samantha Liao <samantha.liao@medicore.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency ask: sequencing of subprocessors + region-pin pledge

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear asks. High-level answers below; I'll follow up with the formal pledge and a proposed subprocessors sequencing plan (PDF/CSV) by Friday.

- Region pinning: Redwood can commit to a primary-region pin for customer production workloads: EU customers -> EU primary, US customers -> US primary, APAC customers -> APAC primary. We will map the primary region to the account's billing/contracting region.
- Transient-egress window (failover): our standard allowance for emergency cross-region failover for primary workloads is up to 48 hours (self-heal objective) for unplanned events. For planned maintenance/capacity optimization we seek to keep any temporary routing within a 4-hour maintenance window, with prior notice.
- Subprocessor sequencing: we will provide a roster CSV with activation triggers and a 10-business-day notification window for new subprocessors that will be used for your account. Critical security subprocessors (KMS, audit-log) will be listed separately and require 15-business-day notice for production activation.

Next steps: Kimberly — can you draft the short pledge statement and the sequencing CSV (include fields: subprocessor_name, role, activation_trigger, notification_period, region_scope, contact)? Rishi — please confirm the KMS locality options we can offer (bring-your-own-key vs Redwood-managed keys) and whether we can offer an EU-resident KMS for Medicore.

Samantha — expect the formal pledge + CSV link by EOD Friday. If that's okay we'll then have legal attach the pledge as an addendum to the DPA.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Strategic Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: subprocessor_roster_2027-04-12.csv
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: pledge language + sequencing CSV (internal)

Team —

I've sketched pledge language below for Marissa to sign. I've also attached an initial sequencing roster (subprocessor_roster_2027-04-12.csv) with two columns called notification_period and activation_trigger. Notes:

- Pledge: "Redwood Inference will designate a single primary geographic region for customer production traffic and will not route customer production data to other regions for the purposes of routine load balancing. In the event of infrastructure outage or emergency failover, Redwood may route traffic to an alternate region for a period not to exceed 48 hours without prior written consent from the customer (except for prolonged outages, where we will seek written approval)."

- On KMS: We can offer an EU-resident managed KMS cluster (separate tenancy) or BYOK with EU keys. Rishi, confirm whether EU-managed KMS will require additional SOC attestation or if current SOC cover is sufficient.

- Sequencing roster: propose these activation tiers:
  Tier 0 — Security-critical (KMS, SIEM, Audit logs): 15-business-day notification; activation only after signed security checklist
  Tier 1 — Core infra (orchestration, autoscaling): 10-business-day notification
  Tier 2 — Analytics & telemetry (non-PII): 5-business-day notification

Marissa: I made the CSV with sample rows. Happy to tighten the wording before we send the pledge to Medicore.

Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Programs, Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_2027-04-12.csv, redline-change-log.txt
From: Samantha Liao <samantha.liao@medicore.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: legal@medicore.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 11:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency ask: sequencing of subprocessors + region-pin pledge

Marissa/Kimberly —

This is helpful, thanks. A couple of clarifying questions from our security team:

- 48 hours is acceptable for emergency failover, but can Redwood commit to a maximum monthly aggregate of transient cross-region traffic (e.g., no more than 0.25% of monthly tokens routed outside the primary for non-emergency maintenance)? Our concern is repeated short failovers that cumulatively violate local residency expectations.

- For the EU-managed KMS option: will Redwood provide key lifecycle logs (rotation, usage) tied to our account and will those logs be covered by the same retention/audit controls in the DPA?

- Regarding notification periods: we need the 10-business-day notification to include a test-plan for new subprocessors and a rollback trigger (example: if data processing tests show >0.01% error on PII tagging). Can you bake that into the sequencing CSV?

If you can incorporate the above into the pledge and csv, our legal team can sign the addendum and we can proceed to legal procurement this month.

Best regards,
Samantha
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Samantha Liao <samantha.liao@medicore.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency ask: sequencing of subprocessors + region-pin pledge (final)

Samantha —

Thanks for the points; we've updated the pledge and CSV to include the specifics you asked for. Summary of final commitments we will include in the addendum:

1) Primary-region pin: EU/US/APAC primary-region mapping as previously stated; routine routing will not cross-map regions.

2) Transient-egress controls: emergency failovers limited to 48 hours per event. In addition, Redwood will commit to a monthly aggregate cap of 0.25% of monthly tokens being routed outside the primary region for non-emergency maintenance activities. We will expose monthly telemetry so you can verify this.

3) Subprocessor sequencing: the roster includes Tier 0/1/2 sequencing and now a required test-plan and rollback trigger field. Notification windows: 15 business days for Tier 0, 10 business days for Tier 1, 5 business days for Tier 2. Activation will not proceed until the test-plan passes acceptance criteria or a rollback is in place.

4) KMS residency: Redwood can offer an EU-resident managed KMS for your account. We will provide key usage and rotation logs (read-only export) tied to your account; logs will be kept under the DPA retention terms and included in audit packages. BYOK remains an option if you require stored-only keys in your HSM.

5) Operational transparency: we'll provide a shared dashboard link (Drive link included in final addendum) showing monthly cross-region telemetry, subprocessor activation history, and KMS audit exports.

Attached are: the final pledge (short statement suitable for signing), the updated CSV (with test-plan and rollback_trigger columns), and a small change log. Please pass to legal for the DPA addendum. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you want to run through the pledge line-by-line.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Strategic Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Medicore_DPA_redline_v3.pdf, subprocessor_roster_2027-04-12.csv, redline-change-log.txt
